subject: Cygnus: scope of non-training data, subprocessor notice and execution plan
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@cygnushealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cygnushealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Cygnus DPA redline: non-training definition + subprocessors

Priyom,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our redline (Cygnus_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf). High level items we need to resolve before procurement can push DocuSign: 

- A tight definition of "Non-Training Customer Data" with examples (PHI, original clinician notes, device telemetry tied to patient identifiers).
- A clear, affirmative prohibition on using Non-Training Customer Data to train or fine-tune models; we are OK with aggregated telemetry for system health but not weight updates.
- Subprocessor notification: we prefer a 7-calendar-day notice for new subprocessors; minimally 30 days but ability to object.
- Cross-border transfers: explicit reliance on SCCs or customer-approved mechanisms; no unilateral determination by Provider.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a named "non-training" carve-out and the SCC language, and whether you can expedite signature? Procurement is sitting on this.

Morgan Lee
Head of Procurement, Cygnus Health

Subject: Proposed language: Non-Training Customer Data + subprocessors

Morgan/Priyom,

Below is proposed text we think is narrow and implementable. The goal is to ensure Cygnus's sensitive categories are excluded from training while allowing Redwood to operate and troubleshoot in production. Please review and mark any lines you need tightened.

PROPOSED CLAUSES (redline-ready):
1) Definition "Non-Training Customer Data" means Customer Data that: (i) constitutes protected health information (PHI) or other specially protected categories under applicable law; (ii) contains original clinical notes or medical device telemetry that is linked to an identified or identifiable individual; or (iii) is otherwise expressly designated in writing by Customer as Non-Training Customer Data. Generated model outputs, de-identified derivatives, and aggregated system metrics are not Non-Training Customer Data unless they include data described in (i)-(iii).

2) Use Limitation Provider will not use Non-Training Customer Data to train, fine-tune, improve, or update Provider models, model weights, or underlying training corpora. Provider may use Non-Training Customer Data for troubleshooting, debugging, security incident investigation, or to satisfy legal obligations, provided such use is limited to the minimum necessary and, where feasible, data is pseudonymized and/or aggregated.

3) Subprocessors & Transfers (a) Provider will comply with Customer-approved transfer mechanisms and will rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or another Customer-specified lawful transfer mechanism for EU-origin data prior to transfer. (b) Provider will provide notice of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding and will accept Customer objections within a 14-day review period for subprocessors designated by Customer as high risk. If Customer requires a 7-day notice for a named subprocessor, Provider will use reasonable commercial efforts to expedite review for that subprocessor only.

Operational note: a blanket 7-day notification for all subprocessors is operationally difficult due to procurement windows with our cloud vendors, but we can support expedited review for a short list of Cygnus-critical processors.

If this looks OK, Priyom will circulate a clean DPA and we can route it for signature (DocuSign).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@cygnushealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed language: Non-Training Customer Data + subprocessors

Lauren/Priyom,

Thanks for the detailed drafting. Two small clarifications from Cygnus: (1) we want an explicit sentence stating that derivative outputs (e.g., model-generated summaries) that include verbatim PHI or clinician notes are treated as Non-Training Customer Data if retained by Provider; (2) for transfers, please include a commitment that Provider will not transfer EU-origin data to countries without an adequate mechanism unless Customer has signed off.

If you can add those two lines, procurement will approve and we can DocuSign the final. We do have a short list of 3 critical subprocessors for which we need 7-day notice: (a) AWS EU logging cluster, (b) Datadog EU metrics, (c) TrustLog audit service. If Redwood can commit to fast-track those, we can accept the 30/14 structure for others.

Morgan

Morgan —

Appreciate the clarifications. We've incorporated both points into the final draft: added a line clarifying that generated summaries or derivative outputs that contain verbatim PHI or clinician notes will be treated as Non-Training Customer Data if retained; and a transfer commitment that Redwood will not transfer EU-origin Customer Data to jurisdictions lacking an adequate transfer mechanism absent Customer27s prior written consent.

On subprocessors: we will accept a 30-day notice plus 14-day objection period for high-risk subprocessors, and we will expedite notice for your named critical subprocessors (AWS EU logging cluster, Datadog EU metrics, TrustLog). We'll provide the expedited notice as soon as those engagements are scheduled.

Next step: I'll send the clean DPA to DocuSign (envelope: https://docusign.com/envelopes/12345ABCDEF) and copy procurement. Expect the signature request later today.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
